html: Chaparra is the name of a small Indigenous group of the southern Ecuadorian highlands and western slopes, in what is now Loja and El Oro provinces, known from Spanish records of the 1500s. They lived near the Palta and Malacatos peoples and may have spoken a related language, now lost. The region was conquered by the Inca in the late 1400s and by the Spanish soon after 1532, as part of what became Ecuador. Little else is known about them.
